Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 90, verse 1–7:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is His mention and sanctified are His names: ﴿I do not swear by this city, and you are a resident of this city, and by the begetter and what he begot, indeed We created man in toil. Does he think that no one has power over him? He says, "I have squandered wealth in abundance." Does he think that no one has seen him?﴾.

His saying, dhikruhu: "I swear, O Muhammad, by this sacred city, which is Makkah, and so the people of interpretation have said."

Those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿I do not swear by this city﴾, meaning: Makkah.

* Abu Kurayb related to us, he said: Waki' related to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Mujahid, ﴿I do not swear by this city﴾, he said: Makkah.

* Ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, ﴿I do not swear by this city﴾, he said: the sacred one.

* Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Mujahid, ﴿I do not swear by this city﴾, he said: Makkah.

* Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, ﴿I do not swear by this city﴾, he said: the city is Makkah.

* Sawwar ibn 'Abd Allah related to us, he said: Yahya ibn Sa'id related to us, from 'Abd al-Malik, from 'Ata', regarding His saying: ﴿I do not swear by this city﴾, meaning Makkah.

* Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the saying of God: ﴿I do not swear by this city﴾, he said: Makkah.

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿and you are a resident of this city﴾

Meaning: in Makkah. His mention, exalted is He, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): "And you, O Muhammad, are a resident (ḥill) of this city, meaning Makkah." That is: you are permitted in it, doing in it what you wish, killing whom you wish to kill and capturing whom you wish to capture, that being absolutely permitted to you. It is said of it: he is ḥill and he is ḥalāl (lawful), he is ḥirm and he is ḥarām (sacred/forbidden), he is muḥill and he is muḥrim, and we permitted (aḥlalnā) and we sanctified (aḥramnā).

The people of interpretation have said something similar to what we have said.

Those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, ﴿and you are a resident of this city﴾, meaning by it: the Prophet of God (ﷺ). God permitted him on the day he entered Makkah to kill whom he wished and to spare whom he wished; so on that day Ibn Khatal was killed in cold blood while clinging to the curtains of the Ka'bah. Afterward, it was not lawful for anyone among the people after the Messenger of God (ﷺ) to kill in it anyone whom God has made sacred. God made lawful for him what he did to the people of Makkah. Have you not heard that God said concerning the sanctity of the Sacred Precinct: ﴿And for God, upon the people, is the pilgrimage to the House, for whoever is able to make his way to it﴾? By "the people" He means the people of the qiblah.

* Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Mujahid, ﴿and you are a resident of this city﴾, he said: whatever you do, you are in permission regarding the matter of fighting.

* Ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, ﴿and you are a resident of this city﴾, he said: what he did in it was made lawful for the Messenger of God (ﷺ) for an hour.

* Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Jarir related to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, ﴿and you are a resident of this city﴾, he said: He made lawful for him to do in it whatever he wished.

* Abu Kurayb related to us, he said: Waki' related to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, ﴿and you are a resident of this city﴾, he said: it was made lawful for the Prophet (ﷺ), he said: do in it whatever you wish.

* Musa ibn 'Abd al-Rahman related to me, he said: Husayn al-Ju'fi related to us, from Za'idah, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding the saying of God ﴿and you are a resident of this city﴾, he said: you are lawful (ḥill) regarding what you do in it.

* Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Hakkam related to us, from 'Amr, from Mansur, from Mujahid, ﴿and you are a resident of this city﴾, he said: God made lawful for you, O Muhammad, whatever you did in this city of anything, meaning Makkah.

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, he said: Abu 'Asim related to us, he said: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, ﴿and you are a resident of this city﴾, he said: you will not be held accountable for what you did in it, and there is not upon you in it what is upon people.

* Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, ﴿and you are a resident of this city﴾, he says: free of sin and wrongdoing.

* Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, ﴿and you are a resident of this city﴾, he says: you are lawful in it, you are not sinful.

* Yunus related to us, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿and you are a resident of this city﴾, he said: No one in it was lawful except the Prophet (ﷺ); everyone who was in it was sacred, and it was not lawful for them to fight in it or to violate its sanctity; so God made it lawful for His Messenger, and he fought the polytheists in it.

* Sawwar ibn 'Abd Allah related to us, he said: Yahya ibn Sa'id related to us, from 'Abd al-Malik, from 'Ata', ﴿and you are a resident of this city﴾, he said: Indeed God sanctified Makkah; it was not made lawful for any prophet except your Prophet, for an hour of a day.

* I was told on the authority of al-Husayn, he said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd related to us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: ﴿and you are a resident of this city﴾, meaning Muhammad, saying: you are lawful within the Sanctuary; kill if you wish, or leave.

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿and the begetter and what he begot﴾

His mention, exalted is He, says: Then He swears by the begetter and by his offspring who was begotten.

Then the people of interpretation differed regarding who is meant by "the begetter and what he begot." Some of them said: "the begetter" refers to every father, and "what he begot" refers to every barren one who has not given birth.

Those who said that:

* Abu Kurayb related to us, he said: Ibn 'Atiyyah related to us, from Sharik, from Khusayf, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿and the begetter and what he begot﴾, he said: "the begetter" is the one who begets, and "what he begot" is the barren one who cannot bear children.

* Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Khusayf, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, ﴿and the begetter and what he begot﴾, he said: the barren one, and the one who gives birth.

* Abu Kurayb related to us, he said: Waki' related to us, from al-Nadr ibn 'Arabi, from 'Ikrimah, ﴿and the begetter and what he begot﴾, he said: the barren one, and the one who gives birth.

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, ﴿and the begetter and what he begot﴾, he said: it is the father and his offspring.

Others said: what is meant by this is Adam and his offspring.

Those who said that:

* Zakariyya ibn Yahya ibn Abi Za'idah related to me, he said: Abu 'Asim related to us, he said: 'Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, ﴿and the begetter and what he begot﴾, he said: "the begetter" is Adam, and "what he begot" is his offspring.

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, he said: Abu 'Asim related to us, he said: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, his saying: ﴿and the begetter and what he begot﴾, he said: his offspring.

* Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, ﴿and the begetter and what he begot﴾, he said: Adam and what he begot.

* Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, ﴿and the begetter and what he begot﴾, he said: Adam and what he begot.

* Abu Kurayb related to us, he said: Ibn Abi Za'idah related to us, from Ibn Abi Khalid, from Abu Salih, regarding the saying of God ﴿and the begetter and what he begot﴾, he said: Adam and what he begot.

* I was told on the authority of al-Husayn, he said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd related to us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say, regarding His saying ﴿and the begetter and what he begot﴾, he said: the begetter is Adam, and what he begot is his offspring.

* Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, his saying ﴿and the begetter and what he begot﴾, he said: Adam and what he begot.

* Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to me, he said: Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd related to us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Abu Salih, regarding His saying ﴿and the begetter and what he begot﴾, he said: Adam and what he begot.

Others said: what is meant by this is Abraham and what he begot.

Those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn Musa al-Harashi related to me, he said: Ja'far ibn Sulayman related to us, he said: I heard Abu 'Imran al-Jawni recite: ﴿and the begetter and what he begot﴾, and he said: Abraham and what he begot.

The correct view on this matter is what those said who said: God swore by every begetter and his offspring, because God generalized "every begetter and what he begot." It is not permissible to restrict this except by a proof that must be accepted, whether from a report or from reason, and there is no report specifying this, nor any demonstrative proof requiring acceptance of its specification; so it remains general as He made it general.

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, We created man in toil﴾

This is the answer to the oath.

* Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, he said: The oath occurs here: ﴿Indeed, We created man in toil﴾.

The people of interpretation differed regarding its meaning. Some of them said: its meaning is: Indeed, We created the son of Adam in hardship, distress and fatigue.

Those who said that:

* 'Ali related to us, he said: Abu Salih related to us, he said: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿Indeed, We created man in toil﴾, he says: in fatigue.

* Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Mansur ibn Zadhan, from al-Hasan, that he said regarding this verse ﴿Indeed, We created man in toil﴾, he says: in hardship.

* Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, ﴿Indeed, We created man in toil﴾, when he was created in hardship; the son of Adam meets nothing but struggling with the affairs of this world and the Hereafter.

* Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿in toil﴾, he said: he struggles with the affairs of this world and the Hereafter.

Others said: He created a creation that We did not create any creature like.

Those who said that:

* Abu Kurayb related to us, he said: Waki' related to us, from 'Ali ibn Rifa'ah, he said: I heard al-Hasan say: God did not create any creature that struggles with what the son of Adam struggles with.

* He said: Waki' related to us, from 'Ali ibn Rifa'ah, he said: I heard Sa'id ibn Abi al-Hasan say: ﴿Indeed, We created man in toil﴾, he said: he struggles with the calamities of this world and the severities of the Hereafter.

* He said: Waki' related to us, from al-Nadr, from 'Ikrimah, he said: ﴿Indeed, We created man in toil﴾, he said: in hardship.

* Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from 'Ata', from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, ﴿Indeed, We created man in toil﴾, he said: in hardship.

* He said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Jurayj, from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas, he said: in the hardship of his livelihood, his carrying, his life, and the growth of his teeth.

* He said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, he said: Mujahid said: ﴿man in toil﴾, he said: the hardship of the emergence of his teeth.

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, he said: Abu 'Asim related to us, he said: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, his saying: ﴿man in toil﴾, he said: hardship.

Others said: the meaning of that is that he was created upright, of balanced stature.

Those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, His saying: ﴿Indeed, We created man in toil﴾, he said: in uprightness; it is also said: in hardship.

* Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, he said: Harmi ibn 'Umarah related to us, he said: Shu'bah related to us, he said: 'Imarah informed me, from 'Ikrimah, regarding His saying ﴿Indeed, We created man in toil﴾, he said: in uprightness, meaning the stature.

* Ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim ﴿Indeed, We created man in toil﴾, he said: upright.

* Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Mihran related to us; and Abu Kurayb related to us, he said: Waki' related to us, both from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, the same.

* Abu Kurayb related to us, he said: Ibn Abi Za'idah related to us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from 'Abd Allah ibn Shaddad, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, We created man in toil﴾, he said: upright in stature; Abu Salih said: upright in stature.

* Yahya ibn Dawud al-Wasiti related to us, he said: Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan related to us, from Isma'il, from Abu Salih ﴿We created man in toil﴾, he said: standing.

* I was told on the authority of al-Husayn, he said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd related to us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say, regarding His saying ﴿in toil﴾: he was created upright on two legs; no other creature was created like his creation.

* Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Jarir related to us, from Mughirah, from Mujahid ﴿Indeed, We created man in toil﴾, he said: in ascent.

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is that he was created in the sky.

Those who said that:

* Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿Indeed, We created man in toil﴾, he said: in the sky, which is called "kabad."

The most correct of these views is the view of those who said: its meaning is that he was created to struggle with matters and to deal with them, so His saying ﴿in toil﴾ means: in hardship.

We have said that this is more correct because this is the well-known meaning of "kabad" in the speech of the Arabs, and from it is the saying of Labid ibn Rabi'ah:

"O eye, why did you not weep for Arbad when we stood and the litigants stood in kabad..." [[That is, the need of the first of them is like the need of the second, and therefore it was necessary to repeat it. Context of the phrase: "It was known that the need of each word... and it was known that the correct view is that it be with it... and it was clear..." to the end of the paragraph.]]

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿Does he think that no one has power over him?﴾

It is mentioned that this was revealed concerning a specific man from the clan of Jumah, who was called Abu al-Ashudd, and he was very strong. So His mention, exalted is He, said: Does this strong one, by his might and power, think that no one will overpower him and defeat him? God is the one who overcomes him and overpowers him.

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿He says, "I have squandered wealth in abundance"﴾

This stout one says: I have squandered much wealth in enmity toward Muhammad (ﷺ), spending it on that; and he is lying in saying so. It is a verb from "talabbud," which means abundance, piled one upon another. It is said: labada bi-l-ard, yalbudu, when it clung to the ground.

The people of interpretation have said something similar to what we have said.

Those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿wealth in abundance﴾, he meant by "labad": abundant wealth.

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, he said: Abu 'Asim related to us, he said: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, ﴿wealth in abundance﴾, he said: abundant.

* Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Muslim informed me, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿I have squandered wealth in abundance﴾, he said: abundant wealth.

* Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, his saying ﴿I have squandered wealth in abundance﴾: i.e., much.

* Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, the same.

* Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿wealth in abundance﴾, he said: "labad" means abundant.

The readers differed in reading this. The majority of the readers of the regions recited ﴿labadan﴾ with the ba' unstressed. Abu Ja'far read it with the ba' stressed.

The correct reading is with it unstressed, because the proof is in consensus upon it.

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿Does he think that no one has seen him?﴾

His mention, exalted is He, says: Does this one who says "I have squandered wealth in abundance" think that no one saw him in the state of spending it, though he claims he spent it?

Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, ﴿Does he think that no one has seen him?﴾: Son of Adam, you will be questioned about this wealth: from where did you acquire it, and where did you spend it.

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, the same.

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, We created man in toil﴾

* Abu Kurayb related to us, he said: Ibn Abi Za'idah related to us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from 'Abd Allah ibn Shaddad, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, We created man in toil﴾, he said: upright in stature; Abu Salih said: upright in stature.

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is that he was created in the sky.

Those who said that:

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿Does he think that no one has power over him?﴾

It is mentioned that this was revealed concerning a specific man from the clan of Jumah, who was called Abu al-Ashudd, and he was very strong. So His mention, exalted is He, said: Does this strong one, by his might and power, think that no one will overpower him and defeat him? God is the one who overcomes him and overpowers him.

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿He says, "I have squandered wealth in abundance"﴾

This stout one says: I have squandered much wealth in enmity toward Muhammad (ﷺ), spending it on that; and he is lying in saying so. It is a verb from "talabbud," which means abundance, piled one upon another. It is said: labada bi-l-ard, yalbudu, when it clung to the ground.

The people of interpretation have said something similar to what we have said.

Those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿wealth in abundance﴾, he meant by "labad": abundant wealth.

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, he said: Abu 'Asim related to us, he said: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, ﴿wealth in abundance﴾, he said: abundant.

* Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Muslim informed me, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿I have squandered wealth in abundance﴾, he said: abundant wealth.

* Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, his saying ﴿I have squandered wealth in abundance﴾: i.e., much.

* Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, the same.

* Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿wealth in abundance﴾, he said: "labad" means abundant.

The readers differed in reading this. The majority of the readers of the regions recited ﴿labadan﴾ with the ba' unstressed. Abu Ja'far read it with the ba' stressed.

The correct reading is with it unstressed, because the proof is in consensus upon it.

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿Does he think that no one has seen him?﴾

His mention, exalted is He, says: Does this one who says "I have squandered wealth in abundance" think that no one saw him in the state of spending it, though he claims he spent it?

Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, ﴿Does he think that no one has seen him?﴾: Son of Adam, you will be questioned about this wealth: from where did you acquire it, and where did you spend it.

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, the same.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 90, verse 1–7:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is His mention and sanctified are His names: ﴿I do not swear by this city, and you are a resident of this city, and by the begetter and what he begot, indeed We created man in toil. Does he think that no one has power over him? He says, "I have squandered wealth in abundance." Does he think that no one has seen him?﴾.

His saying, dhikruhu: "I swear, O Muhammad, by this sacred city, which is Makkah, and so the people of interpretation have said."

Those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿I do not swear by this city﴾, meaning: Makkah.

* Abu Kurayb related to us, he said: Waki' related to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Mujahid, ﴿I do not swear by this city﴾, he said: Makkah.

* Ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, ﴿I do not swear by this city﴾, he said: the sacred one.

* Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Mujahid, ﴿I do not swear by this city﴾, he said: Makkah.

* Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, ﴿I do not swear by this city﴾, he said: the city is Makkah.

* Sawwar ibn 'Abd Allah related to us, he said: Yahya ibn Sa'id related to us, from 'Abd al-Malik, from 'Ata', regarding His saying: ﴿I do not swear by this city﴾, meaning Makkah.

* Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the saying of God: ﴿I do not swear by this city﴾, he said: Makkah.

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿and you are a resident of this city﴾

Meaning: in Makkah. His mention, exalted is He, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): "And you, O Muhammad, are a resident (ḥill) of this city, meaning Makkah." That is: you are permitted in it, doing in it what you wish, killing whom you wish to kill and capturing whom you wish to capture, that being absolutely permitted to you. It is said of it: he is ḥill and he is ḥalāl (lawful), he is ḥirm and he is ḥarām (sacred/forbidden), he is muḥill and he is muḥrim, and we permitted (aḥlalnā) and we sanctified (aḥramnā).

The people of interpretation have said something similar to what we have said.

Those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, ﴿and you are a resident of this city﴾, meaning by it: the Prophet of God (ﷺ). God permitted him on the day he entered Makkah to kill whom he wished and to spare whom he wished; so on that day Ibn Khatal was killed in cold blood while clinging to the curtains of the Ka'bah. Afterward, it was not lawful for anyone among the people after the Messenger of God (ﷺ) to kill in it anyone whom God has made sacred. God made lawful for him what he did to the people of Makkah. Have you not heard that God said concerning the sanctity of the Sacred Precinct: ﴿And for God, upon the people, is the pilgrimage to the House, for whoever is able to make his way to it﴾? By "the people" He means the people of the qiblah.

* Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Mujahid, ﴿and you are a resident of this city﴾, he said: whatever you do, you are in permission regarding the matter of fighting.

* Ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, ﴿and you are a resident of this city﴾, he said: what he did in it was made lawful for the Messenger of God (ﷺ) for an hour.

* Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Jarir related to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, ﴿and you are a resident of this city﴾, he said: He made lawful for him to do in it whatever he wished.

* Abu Kurayb related to us, he said: Waki' related to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, ﴿and you are a resident of this city﴾, he said: it was made lawful for the Prophet (ﷺ), he said: do in it whatever you wish.

* Musa ibn 'Abd al-Rahman related to me, he said: Husayn al-Ju'fi related to us, from Za'idah, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding the saying of God ﴿and you are a resident of this city﴾, he said: you are lawful (ḥill) regarding what you do in it.

* Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Hakkam related to us, from 'Amr, from Mansur, from Mujahid, ﴿and you are a resident of this city﴾, he said: God made lawful for you, O Muhammad, whatever you did in this city of anything, meaning Makkah.

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, he said: Abu 'Asim related to us, he said: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, ﴿and you are a resident of this city﴾, he said: you will not be held accountable for what you did in it, and there is not upon you in it what is upon people.

* Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, ﴿and you are a resident of this city﴾, he says: free of sin and wrongdoing.

* Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, ﴿and you are a resident of this city﴾, he says: you are lawful in it, you are not sinful.

* Yunus related to us, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿and you are a resident of this city﴾, he said: No one in it was lawful except the Prophet (ﷺ); everyone who was in it was sacred, and it was not lawful for them to fight in it or to violate its sanctity; so God made it lawful for His Messenger, and he fought the polytheists in it.

* Sawwar ibn 'Abd Allah related to us, he said: Yahya ibn Sa'id related to us, from 'Abd al-Malik, from 'Ata', ﴿and you are a resident of this city﴾, he said: Indeed God sanctified Makkah; it was not made lawful for any prophet except your Prophet, for an hour of a day.

* I was told on the authority of al-Husayn, he said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd related to us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: ﴿and you are a resident of this city﴾, meaning Muhammad, saying: you are lawful within the Sanctuary; kill if you wish, or leave.

As for His saying: ﴿Does he think that no one has power over him?﴾

It is mentioned that this was revealed concerning a specific man from the clan of Jumah, who was called Abu al-Ashudd, and he was very strong. So His mention, exalted is He, said: Does this strong one, by his might and power, think that no one will overpower him and defeat him? God is the one who overcomes him and overpowers him.

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿He says, "I have squandered wealth in abundance"﴾

This stout one says: I have squandered much wealth in enmity toward Muhammad (ﷺ), spending it on that; and he is lying in saying so. It is a verb from "talabbud," which means abundance, piled one upon another. It is said: labada bi-l-ard, yalbudu, when it clung to the ground.

The people of interpretation have said something similar to what we have said.

Those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿wealth in abundance﴾, he meant by "labad": abundant wealth.

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, he said: Abu 'Asim related to us, he said: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, ﴿wealth in abundance﴾, he said: abundant.

* Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Muslim informed me, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿I have squandered wealth in abundance﴾, he said: abundant wealth.

* Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, his saying ﴿I have squandered wealth in abundance﴾: i.e., much.

* Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, the same.

* Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿wealth in abundance﴾, he said: "labad" means abundant.

The readers differed in reading this. The majority of the readers of the regions recited ﴿labadan﴾ with the ba' unstressed. Abu Ja'far read it with the ba' stressed.

The correct reading is with it unstressed, because the proof is in consensus upon it.

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿Does he think that no one has seen him?﴾

His mention, exalted is He, says: Does this one who says "I have squandered wealth in abundance" think that no one saw him in the state of spending it, though he claims he spent it?

Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, ﴿Does he think that no one has seen him?﴾: Son of Adam, you will be questioned about this wealth: from where did you acquire it, and where did you spend it.

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, the same.

Does he think that no one has power over him? He says, "I have squandered wealth in abundance." Does he think that no one has seen him?﴾.

His saying, dhikruhu: "I swear, O Muhammad, by this sacred city, which is Makkah, and so the people of interpretation have said."

As for His saying: ﴿and you are a resident of this city﴾

Meaning: in Makkah. His mention, exalted is He, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): "And you, O Muhammad, are a resident (ḥill) of this city, meaning Makkah." That is: you are permitted in it, doing in it what you wish, killing whom you wish to kill and capturing whom you wish to capture, that being absolutely permitted to you. It is said of it: he is ḥill and he is ḥalāl (lawful), he is ḥirm and he is ḥarām (sacred/forbidden), he is muḥill and he is muḥrim, and we permitted (aḥlalnā) and we sanctified (aḥramnā).

The people of interpretation have said something similar to what we have said.

Those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, ﴿and you are a resident of this city﴾, meaning by it: the Prophet of God (ﷺ). God permitted him on the day he entered Makkah to kill whom he wished and to spare whom he wished; so on that day Ibn Khatal was killed in cold blood while clinging to the curtains of the Ka'bah. Afterward, it was not lawful for anyone among the people after the Messenger of God (ﷺ) to kill in it anyone whom God has made sacred. God made lawful for him what he did to the people of Makkah. Have you not heard that God said concerning the sanctity of the Sacred Precinct: ﴿And for God, upon the people, is the pilgrimage to the House, for whoever is able to make his way to it﴾? By "the people" He means the people of the qiblah.

* Yunus related to us, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿and you are a resident of this city﴾, he said: No one in it was lawful except the Prophet (ﷺ); everyone who was in it was sacred, and it was not lawful for them to fight in it or to violate its sanctity; so God made it lawful for His Messenger, and he fought the polytheists in it.

* * *

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿and the begetter and what he begot﴾

His mention, exalted is He, says: Then He swears by the begetter and by his offspring who was begotten.

Then the people of interpretation differed regarding who is meant by "the begetter and what he begot." Some of them said: "the begetter" refers to every father, and "what he begot" refers to every barren one who has not given birth.

Those who said that:

* Abu Kurayb related to us, he said: Ibn 'Atiyyah related to us, from Sharik, from Khusayf, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿and the begetter and what he begot﴾, he said: "the begetter" is the one who begets, and "what he begot" is the barren one who cannot bear children.

* Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Khusayf, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, ﴿and the begetter and what he begot﴾, he said: the barren one, and the one who gives birth.

* Abu Kurayb related to us, he said: Waki' related to us, from al-Nadr ibn 'Arabi, from 'Ikrimah, ﴿and the begetter and what he begot﴾, he said: the barren one, and the one who gives birth.

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, ﴿and the begetter and what he begot﴾, he said: it is the father and his offspring.

Others said: what is meant by this is Adam and his offspring.

Those who said that:

* Zakariyya ibn Yahya ibn Abi Za'idah related to me, he said: Abu 'Asim related to us, he said: 'Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, ﴿and the begetter and what he begot﴾, he said: "the begetter" is Adam, and "what he begot" is his offspring.

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, he said: Abu 'Asim related to us, he said: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, his saying: ﴿and the begetter and what he begot﴾, he said: his offspring.

* Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, ﴿and the begetter and what he begot﴾, he said: Adam and what he begot.

* Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, ﴿and the begetter and what he begot﴾, he said: Adam and what he begot.

* Abu Kurayb related to us, he said: Ibn Abi Za'idah related to us, from Ibn Abi Khalid, from Abu Salih, regarding the saying of God ﴿and the begetter and what he begot﴾, he said: Adam and what he begot.

* I was told on the authority of al-Husayn, he said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd related to us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say, regarding His saying ﴿and the begetter and what he begot﴾, he said: the begetter is Adam, and what he begot is his offspring.

* Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, his saying ﴿and the begetter and what he begot﴾, he said: Adam and what he begot.

* Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to me, he said: Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd related to us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Abu Salih, regarding His saying ﴿and the begetter and what he begot﴾, he said: Adam and what he begot.

Others said: what is meant by this is Abraham and what he begot.

Those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn Musa al-Harashi related to me, he said: Ja'far ibn Sulayman related to us, he said: I heard Abu 'Imran al-Jawni recite: ﴿and the begetter and what he begot﴾, and he said: Abraham and what he begot.

The correct view on this matter is what those said who said: God swore by every begetter and his offspring, because God generalized "every begetter and what he begot." It is not permissible to restrict this except by a proof that must be accepted, whether from a report or from reason, and there is no report specifying this, nor any demonstrative proof requiring acceptance of its specification; so it remains general as He made it general.

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, We created man in toil﴾

This is the answer to the oath.

* Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, he said: The oath occurs here: ﴿Indeed, We created man in toil﴾.

The people of interpretation differed regarding its meaning. Some of them said: its meaning is: Indeed, We created the son of Adam in hardship, distress and fatigue.

Those who said that:

* 'Ali related to us, he said: Abu Salih related to us, he said: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿Indeed, We created man in toil﴾, he says: in fatigue.

* Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Mansur ibn Zadhan, from al-Hasan, that he said regarding this verse ﴿Indeed, We created man in toil﴾, he says: in hardship.

* Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, ﴿Indeed, We created man in toil﴾, when he was created in hardship; the son of Adam meets nothing but struggling with the affairs of this world and the Hereafter.

* Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿in toil﴾, he said: he struggles with the affairs of this world and the Hereafter.

Others said: He created a creation that We did not create any creature like.

Those who said that:

* Abu Kurayb related to us, he said: Waki' related to us, from 'Ali ibn Rifa'ah, he said: I heard al-Hasan say: God did not create any creature that struggles with what the son of Adam struggles with.

* He said: Waki' related to us, from 'Ali ibn Rifa'ah, he said: I heard Sa'id ibn Abi al-Hasan say: ﴿Indeed, We created man in toil﴾, he said: he struggles with the calamities of this world and the severities of the Hereafter.

* He said: Waki' related to us, from al-Nadr, from 'Ikrimah, he said: ﴿Indeed, We created man in toil﴾, he said: in hardship.

* Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from 'Ata', from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, ﴿Indeed, We created man in toil﴾, he said: in hardship.

* He said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Jurayj, from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas, he said: in the hardship of his livelihood, his carrying, his life, and the growth of his teeth.

* He said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, he said: Mujahid said: ﴿man in toil﴾, he said: the hardship of the emergence of his teeth.

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, he said: Abu 'Asim related to us, he said: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, his saying: ﴿man in toil﴾, he said: hardship.

Others said: the meaning of that is that he was created upright, of balanced stature.

Those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, His saying: ﴿Indeed, We created man in toil﴾, he said: in uprightness; it is also said: in hardship.

* Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, he said: Harmi ibn 'Umarah related to us, he said: Shu'bah related to us, he said: 'Imarah informed me, from 'Ikrimah, regarding His saying ﴿Indeed, We created man in toil﴾, he said: in uprightness, meaning the stature.

* Ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim ﴿Indeed, We created man in toil﴾, he said: upright.

* Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Mihran related to us; and Abu Kurayb related to us, he said: Waki' related to us, both from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, the same.

* Abu Kurayb related to us, he said: Ibn Abi Za'idah related to us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from 'Abd Allah ibn Shaddad, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, We created man in toil﴾, he said: upright in stature; Abu Salih said: upright in stature.

* Yahya ibn Dawud al-Wasiti related to us, he said: Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan related to us, from Isma'il, from Abu Salih ﴿We created man in toil﴾, he said: standing.

* I was told on the authority of al-Husayn, he said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd related to us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say, regarding His saying ﴿in toil﴾: he was created upright on two legs; no other creature was created like his creation.

* Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Jarir related to us, from Mughirah, from Mujahid ﴿Indeed, We created man in toil﴾, he said: in ascent.

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is that he was created in the sky.

Those who said that:

* Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿Indeed, We created man in toil﴾, he said: in the sky, which is called "kabad."

The most correct of these views is the view of those who said: its meaning is that he was created to struggle with matters and to deal with them, so His saying ﴿in toil﴾ means: in hardship.

We have said that this is more correct because this is the well-known meaning of "kabad" in the speech of the Arabs, and from it is the saying of Labid ibn Rabi'ah:

"O eye, why did you not weep for Arbad when we stood and the litigants stood in kabad..." [[That is, the need of the first of them is like the need of the second, and therefore it was necessary to repeat it. Context of the phrase: "It was known that the need of each word... and it was known that the correct view is that it be with it... and it was clear..." to the end of the paragraph.]]

As for His saying: ﴿Does he think that no one has power over him?﴾

It is mentioned that this was revealed concerning a specific man from the clan of Jumah, who was called Abu al-Ashudd, and he was very strong. So His mention, exalted is He, said: Does this strong one, by his might and power, think that no one will overpower him and defeat him? God is the one who overcomes him and overpowers him.

As for His saying: ﴿He says, "I have squandered wealth in abundance"﴾

This stout one says: I have squandered much wealth in enmity toward Muhammad (ﷺ), spending it on that; and he is lying in saying so. It is a verb from "talabbud," which means abundance, piled one upon another. It is said: labada bi-l-ard, yalbudu, when it clung to the ground.

The people of interpretation have said something similar to what we have said.

Those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿wealth in abundance﴾, he meant by "labad": abundant wealth.

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, he said: Abu 'Asim related to us, he said: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, ﴿wealth in abundance﴾, he said: abundant.

* Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Muslim informed me, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿I have squandered wealth in abundance﴾, he said: abundant wealth.

* Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, his saying ﴿I have squandered wealth in abundance﴾: i.e., much.

* Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, the same.

* Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿wealth in abundance﴾, he said: "labad" means abundant.

The readers differed in reading this. The majority of the readers of the regions recited ﴿labadan﴾ with the ba' unstressed. Abu Ja'far read it with the ba' stressed.

The correct reading is with it unstressed, because the proof is in consensus upon it.

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, We created man in toil﴾

This is the answer to the oath.

Those who said that:

* 'Ali related to us, he said: Abu Salih related to us, he said: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿Indeed, We created man in toil﴾, he says: in fatigue.

As for His saying: ﴿Does he think that no one has power over him?﴾

It is mentioned that this was revealed concerning a specific man from the clan of Jumah, who was called Abu al-Ashudd, and he was very strong. So His mention, exalted is He, said: Does this strong one, by his might and power, think that no one will overpower him and defeat him? God is the one who overcomes him and overpowers him.

As for His saying: ﴿He says, "I have squandered wealth in abundance"﴾

This stout one says: I have squandered much wealth in enmity toward Muhammad (ﷺ), spending it on that; and he is lying in saying so. It is a verb from "talabbud," which means abundance, piled one upon another. It is said: labada bi-l-ard, yalbudu, when it clung to the ground.

The people of interpretation have said something similar to what we have said.

Those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿wealth in abundance﴾, he meant by "labad": abundant wealth.

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, he said: Abu 'Asim related to us, he said: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, ﴿wealth in abundance﴾, he said: abundant.

* Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Muslim informed me, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿I have squandered wealth in abundance﴾, he said: abundant wealth.

* Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, his saying ﴿I have squandered wealth in abundance﴾: i.e., much.

* Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, the same.

* Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿wealth in abundance﴾, he said: "labad" means abundant.

The readers differed in reading this. The majority of the readers of the regions recited ﴿labadan﴾ with the ba' unstressed. Abu Ja'far read it with the ba' stressed.

The correct reading is with it unstressed, because the proof is in consensus upon it.

As for His saying: ﴿Does he think that no one has seen him?﴾

His mention, exalted is He, says: Does this one who says "I have squandered wealth in abundance" think that no one saw him in the state of spending it, though he claims he spent it?

Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, ﴿Does he think that no one has seen him?﴾: Son of Adam, you will be questioned about this wealth: from where did you acquire it, and where did you spend it.

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, the same.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 90, verse 1–7:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is His mention and sanctified are His names: ﴿I do not swear by this city, and you are a resident of this city, and by the begetter and what he begot, indeed We created man in toil. Those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿I do not swear by this city﴾, meaning: Makkah.

* Abu Kurayb related to us, he said: Waki' related to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Mujahid, ﴿I do not swear by this city﴾, he said: Makkah.

* Ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, ﴿I do not swear by this city﴾, he said: the sacred one.

* Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Mujahid, ﴿I do not swear by this city﴾, he said: Makkah.

* Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, ﴿I do not swear by this city﴾, he said: the city is Makkah.

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿and you are a resident of this city﴾

Meaning: in Makkah. His mention, exalted is He, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): "And you, O Muhammad, are a resident (ḥill) of this city, meaning Makkah." That is: you are permitted in it, doing in it what you wish, killing whom you wish to kill and capturing whom you wish to capture, that being absolutely permitted to you. It is said of it: he is ḥill and he is ḥalāl (lawful), he is ḥirm and he is ḥarām (sacred/forbidden), he is muḥill and he is muḥrim, and we permitted (aḥlalnā) and we sanctified (aḥramnā).

The people of interpretation have said something similar to what we have said.

Those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, ﴿and you are a resident of this city﴾, meaning by it: the Prophet of God (ﷺ). God permitted him on the day he entered Makkah to kill whom he wished and to spare whom he wished; so on that day Ibn Khatal was killed in cold blood while clinging to the curtains of the Ka'bah. Afterward, it was not lawful for anyone among the people after the Messenger of God (ﷺ) to kill in it anyone whom God has made sacred. God made lawful for him what he did to the people of Makkah. Have you not heard that God said concerning the sanctity of the Sacred Precinct: ﴿And for God, upon the people, is the pilgrimage to the House, for whoever is able to make his way to it﴾? By "the people" He means the people of the qiblah.

* Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Hakkam related to us, from 'Amr, from Mansur, from Mujahid, ﴿and you are a resident of this city﴾, he said: God made lawful for you, O Muhammad, whatever you did in this city of anything, meaning Makkah.

* Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿in toil﴾, he said: he struggles with the affairs of this world and the Hereafter.

Others said: He created a creation that We did not create any creature like.

Those who said that:

* Abu Kurayb related to us, he said: Waki' related to us, from 'Ali ibn Rifa'ah, he said: I heard al-Hasan say: God did not create any creature that struggles with what the son of Adam struggles with.

* He said: Waki' related to us, from 'Ali ibn Rifa'ah, he said: I heard Sa'id ibn Abi al-Hasan say: ﴿Indeed, We created man in toil﴾, he said: he struggles with the calamities of this world and the severities of the Hereafter.

* He said: Waki' related to us, from al-Nadr, from 'Ikrimah, he said: ﴿Indeed, We created man in toil﴾, he said: in hardship.

* Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from 'Ata', from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, ﴿Indeed, We created man in toil﴾, he said: in hardship.

* He said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Jurayj, from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas, he said: in the hardship of his livelihood, his carrying, his life, and the growth of his teeth.

* He said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, he said: Mujahid said: ﴿man in toil﴾, he said: the hardship of the emergence of his teeth.

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, he said: Abu 'Asim related to us, he said: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, his saying: ﴿man in toil﴾, he said: hardship.

Others said: the meaning of that is that he was created upright, of balanced stature.

Those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, His saying: ﴿Indeed, We created man in toil﴾, he said: in uprightness; it is also said: in hardship.

* Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, he said: Harmi ibn 'Umarah related to us, he said: Shu'bah related to us, he said: 'Imarah informed me, from 'Ikrimah, regarding His saying ﴿Indeed, We created man in toil﴾, he said: in uprightness, meaning the stature.

* Ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim ﴿Indeed, We created man in toil﴾, he said: upright.

* Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Mihran related to us; and Abu Kurayb related to us, he said: Waki' related to us, both from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, the same.

* Abu Kurayb related to us, he said: Ibn Abi Za'idah related to us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from 'Abd Allah ibn Shaddad, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, We created man in toil﴾, he said: upright in stature; Abu Salih said: upright in stature.

* Yahya ibn Dawud al-Wasiti related to us, he said: Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan related to us, from Isma'il, from Abu Salih ﴿We created man in toil﴾, he said: standing.

* I was told on the authority of al-Husayn, he said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd related to us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say, regarding His saying ﴿in toil﴾: he was created upright on two legs; no other creature was created like his creation.

* Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Jarir related to us, from Mughirah, from Mujahid ﴿Indeed, We created man in toil﴾, he said: in ascent.

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is that he was created in the sky.

Those who said that:

* Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿Indeed, We created man in toil﴾, he said: in the sky, which is called "kabad."

The most correct of these views is the view of those who said: its meaning is that he was created to struggle with matters and to deal with them, so His saying ﴿in toil﴾ means: in hardship.

We have said that this is more correct because this is the well-known meaning of "kabad" in the speech of the Arabs, and from it is the saying of Labid ibn Rabi'ah:

"O eye, why did you not weep for Arbad when we stood and the litigants stood in kabad..." [[That is, the need of the first of them is like the need of the second, and therefore it was necessary to repeat it. Context of the phrase: "It was known that the need of each word... and it was known that the correct view is that it be with it... and it was clear..." to the end of the paragraph.]]

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿Does he think that no one has power over him?﴾

It is mentioned that this was revealed concerning a specific man from the clan of Jumah, who was called Abu al-Ashudd, and he was very strong. So His mention, exalted is He, said: Does this strong one, by his might and power, think that no one will overpower him and defeat him? God is the one who overcomes him and overpowers him.

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿He says, "I have squandered wealth in abundance"﴾

This stout one says: I have squandered much wealth in enmity toward Muhammad (ﷺ), spending it on that; and he is lying in saying so. It is a verb from "talabbud," which means abundance, piled one upon another. It is said: labada bi-l-ard, yalbudu, when it clung to the ground.

The people of interpretation have said something similar to what we have said.

Those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿wealth in abundance﴾, he meant by "labad": abundant wealth.

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, he said: Abu 'Asim related to us, he said: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, ﴿wealth in abundance﴾, he said: abundant.

* Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Muslim informed me, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿I have squandered wealth in abundance﴾, he said: abundant wealth.

* Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, his saying ﴿I have squandered wealth in abundance﴾: i.e., much.

* Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, the same.

* Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿wealth in abundance﴾, he said: "labad" means abundant.

The readers differed in reading this. The majority of the readers of the regions recited ﴿labadan﴾ with the ba' unstressed. Abu Ja'far read it with the ba' stressed.

The correct reading is with it unstressed, because the proof is in consensus upon it.

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿Does he think that no one has seen him?﴾

His mention, exalted is He, says: Does this one who says "I have squandered wealth in abundance" think that no one saw him in the state of spending it, though he claims he spent it?

Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, ﴿Does he think that no one has seen him?﴾: Son of Adam, you will be questioned about this wealth: from where did you acquire it, and where did you spend it.

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, the same.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 90, verse 8–16 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Did We not make for him two eyes (8), and a tongue and two lips (9), and guide him to the two highways (10)? But he has not attempted the steep path (11). And what can make you know what the steep path is? (12) It is the freeing of a slave (13), or feeding on a day of severe hunger (14), an orphan of near relationship (15), or a needy person in misery (16).﴾

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: Did We not make for this speaker, ﴿who has squandered wealth in abundance﴾, two eyes with which he sees the proofs of God against him, and a tongue with which he expresses what he wishes, and two lips, a blessing from Us upon him in that regard.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿Did We not make for him two eyes and a tongue and two lips?﴾ — blessings from God in succession, by which He makes you acknowledge, so that you may thank Him.

* *

His saying: ﴿And We guided him to the two highways﴾

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: And We guided him to the two paths, and najd is a path in elevation.

The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of that. Some of them said: By it is meant the highway of good and the highway of evil, as He said: ﴿Indeed, We guided him to the way, whether he be grateful or ungrateful﴾.

Mention of those who said that:

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from 'Asim, from Zirr, from 'Abd Allah, regarding ﴿And We guided him to the two highways﴾, he said: the good and the evil.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from 'Asim, from Zirr, from 'Abd Allah, the like of it.

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Mundhir, from his father, from al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym, who said: "They are not the two breasts."

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us; and Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, saying: 'Imran narrated to us, all from 'Asim, from Zirr, from 'Abd Allah, regarding ﴿And We guided him to the two highways﴾, he said: the highway of good and the highway of evil.

Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Hisham ibn 'Abd al-Malik narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, saying: 'Asim informed me, saying: I heard Abu Wa'il say: 'Abd Allah used to say regarding "And We guided him to the two highways": the highway of good and the highway of evil.

'Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿And We guided him to the two highways﴾, he said: guidance and misguidance.

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, ﴿And We guided him to the two highways﴾, he said: the path of good and evil.

Hannad ibn al-Sarri narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us, from Simak, from 'Ikrimah, regarding His saying: ﴿And We guided him to the two highways﴾, he said: the good and the evil.

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym, from Abu Burdah, who said: al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym passed by us, and we asked him about this verse: ﴿And We guided him to the two highways﴾, and he said: "Indeed, they are not the two breasts."

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Mujahid, who said: the good and the evil.

Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿And We guided him to the two highways﴾, he said: the highway of good and evil.

I was told from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: ﴿And We guided him to the two highways﴾: the highway of good and the highway of evil.

'Imran ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Warith narrated to us, saying: Yunus narrated to us, from al-Hasan, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "They are two highways: the highway of good and the highway of evil, so let the highway of evil not be more beloved to you than the highway of good."

Mujahid ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, saying: 'Atiyyah Abu Wahb informed us, saying: I heard al-Hasan say: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Behold, they are only two highways: the highway of good and the highway of evil, so let the highway of evil not be more beloved to you than the highway of good."

Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Hisham ibn 'Abd al-Malik narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Habib, from al-Hasan, from the Prophet (ﷺ), the like of it.

Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, from Abu Raja', who said: I heard al-Hasan say: ﴿And We guided him to the two highways﴾, and he said: "It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God (ﷺ) used to say: 'O people, they are only the two highways: the highway of good and the highway of evil, so let the highway of evil not be more beloved to you than the highway of good.'"

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿And We guided him to the two highways﴾: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God (ﷺ) used to say: "O people, they are only the two highways: the highway of good and the highway of evil, so let the highway of evil not be more beloved to you than the highway of good."

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Hasan, regarding His saying: ﴿And We guided him to the two highways﴾, he said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "They are only two highways, so let the highway of evil not be more beloved to you than the highway of good."

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding God's saying: ﴿And We guided him to the two highways﴾: "The one who cuts off the road of good and evil." And he recited God's saying: ﴿Indeed, We guided him to the way﴾.

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: And We guided him to the two breasts: the two channels of milk by which he is nourished, and upon which his flesh and body grow.

Mention of those who said that:

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, saying: 'Isa ibn 'Aqal narrated to us, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿And We guided him to the two highways﴾, he said: "They are the two breasts."

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from al-Mubarak ibn Mujahid, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, who said: "The two breasts."

The most correct of the two opinions in this matter, in our view, is the saying of those who said: By it is meant the path of good and evil. This is because there is no saying on this matter that we know of other than the two sayings we have mentioned. Although the two breasts are channels of milk, when God, may His remembrance be exalted, enumerated His blessings upon the servant by His saying: ﴿Indeed, We created man from a drop of mixed sperm, to try him, and made him hearing and seeing. Indeed, We guided him to the way﴾, He was only enumerating His guidance to him to the path of good as one of His blessings. So likewise His saying: ﴿And We guided him to the two highways﴾.

* *

His saying: ﴿But he has not attempted the steep path﴾

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: So he did not ride the steep path, cross it and traverse it.

It was mentioned that al-'Aqabah is a mountain in Hell.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Kathir narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Raja', from al-Hasan, regarding God's saying: ﴿But he has not attempted the steep path﴾, he said: "A steep path in Hell."

Umar ibn Isma'il ibn Mujalid narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Idris narrated to us, from his father, from 'Atiyyah, from Ibn 'Umar, regarding His saying: ﴿But he has not attempted the steep path﴾: "A mountain of Hell."

Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, from Abu Raja', from al-Hasan, regarding His saying: ﴿But he has not attempted the steep path﴾, he said: "Hell."

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, His saying: ﴿But he has not attempted the steep path﴾: "It is a severe ordeal, so attempt it through obedience to God."

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿But he has not attempted the steep path﴾, he said: "For the Fire there is a steep path before the bridge."

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Wahb ibn Jarir narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, saying: I heard Yahya ibn Ayyub narrate from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from Shu'ayb ibn Zur'ah, from Hanash, from Ka'b, that he said: ﴿But he has not attempted the steep path﴾: "It is seventy levels in Hell."

The phrase ﴿But he has not attempted the steep path﴾ is given with "lā" mentioned once, and the Arabs rarely isolate it in speech in such a context unless they repeat it with another statement, as He said: ﴿So he neither believed nor prayed﴾ and ﴿No fear shall be upon them, nor shall they grieve﴾. He only did so in this place, relying on the meaning of the end of the speech, which repeats it once more, namely His saying when explaining the attempt of the steep path: ﴿The freeing of a slave, or feeding on a day of severe hunger, an orphan of near relationship, or a needy person in misery, then he was among those who believed﴾. He explained it by three things, so it was as if it were at the beginning of the speech, saying: "So he did neither this nor that nor that." Ibn Zayd interpreted it in the sense of "afalā" (then will he not), and whoever interprets it that way has no need to claim that something is omitted from the speech.

Report of that from Ibn Zayd:

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, and he recited God's saying: ﴿But he has not attempted the steep path﴾, he said: "Will he not take the road by which there is salvation and good?" Then he said: ﴿And what can make you know what the steep path is?﴾

* *

His saying: ﴿And what can make you know what the steep path is?﴾

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: And what made you aware, O Muhammad, of what the steep path is?

Then He, may His praise be exalted, explained to him what the steep path is, what salvation from it is, and what the manner of attempting it is. So He said: attempting it and crossing it is the freeing of a slave from bondage, and the release from servitude.

As it was narrated:

Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, from Abu Raja', from al-Hasan: ﴿And what can make you know what the steep path is? The freeing of a slave﴾, he said: "It was mentioned to us that there is no Muslim who frees a Muslim slave except that it becomes his ransom from the Fire."

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, His saying: ﴿And what can make you know what the steep path is? The freeing of a slave﴾: "It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God (ﷺ) was asked which of the slaves was greatest in reward? He said: 'The most costly of them.'"

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd narrated to us, from Ma'dan ibn Abi Talhah, from Abu Najih, who said: I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: "Whatever Muslim man frees a Muslim man, God will make every bone of his a ransom for a bone of his liberated one from the Fire; and whatever Muslim woman frees a Muslim woman, God will make every bone of hers a ransom for a bone of her liberated one from the Fire."

[Chain continues:] He said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Qays al-Judhami, from 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir al-Juhani, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Whoever frees a believing slave, it is his ransom from the Fire."

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿And what can make you know what the steep path is?﴾ Then he informed about attempting it, saying: ﴿The freeing of a slave or feeding﴾.

The readers differed in reading this. Some readers of Makkah and most readers of Basrah, from Ibn Abi Ishaq, and among the Kufans, al-Kisa'i, read ﴿fakku raqabatin aw aṭ'ama﴾ [with "aṭ'ama" as a past verb]. Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala used to argue, as has reached me, from His saying: ﴿then he was among those who believed﴾, as if its meaning is: "He was there", so neither freeing a slave nor feeding, then he was among those who believed. Most readers of Madinah, Kufah and Syria read ﴿fakku raqabatin﴾ in the genitive construction, and ﴿aw iṭ'āmun﴾ as a verbal noun.

The correct view on this is that they are two well-known readings, each of which has been read by scholars among the readers, and each has a meaning understood, so whichever reading the reader uses is correct. The reading, if read as a verb, its interpretation is: "He did not attempt the steep path, neither freed a slave nor fed, then he was among those who believed." And "And what can make you know what the steep path is?" is in the sense of wonder and magnification. This reading is better in its Arabic construction, because "iṭ'ām" is a noun, and His saying "then he was among those who believed" is a verb, and the Arabs prefer to match nouns with nouns like them, and verbs with verbs. If the revelation had come as "thumma in kāna min alladhīna āmanū", it would have been better and more fitting with "iṭ'ām" and "fakk" than "thumma kāna". That is why I said: "fakku raqabatin aw aṭ'ama" is more correct in Arabic than the other, although the other also has a known form. Its form is that you hide "an" and then drop it, as Tarafah ibn al-'Abd said:

"Ala ayyuha dhā al-zājirī aḥḍura al-wagha... wa an ashhada al-ladhdhāti hal anta mukhlidī"

meaning: "Ala, O you who restrains me from attending the battle [an uhdura]..." In His saying "an ashhad" is the clear evidence that it is conjoined with another "an" like it that came before it, and that is the reason for its permissibility. When the speech is directed to this form, His saying "fakku raqabatin aw iṭ'āmun" is an explanation of His saying "And what can make you know what the steep path is?", as if it were said: "And what made you know what the steep path is? It is the freeing of a slave, or feeding on a day of severe hunger", just as He, may His praise be exalted, said: "And what can make you know what it is? A fire, blazing", explaining His saying: "Then his mother is the Abyss", and then said: "And what can make you know what the Abyss is? It is a fire, blazing."

* *

His saying: ﴿or feeding on a day of severe hunger﴾

He says: or feeding on a day of hunger, and al-sāghib is the hungry one.

The people of interpretation said similarly to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿or feeding on a day of severe hunger﴾, "a day of famine."

Al-Hasan ibn 'Arafah narrated to us, saying: Khalid ibn Hayyan al-Raqqi Abu Yazid narrated to me, from Ja'far ibn Burqan, from 'Ikrimah regarding God's saying: ﴿or feeding on a day of severe hunger﴾, he said: "a day of famine."

Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿on a day of severe hunger﴾, he said: "The hunger."

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, His saying: ﴿or feeding on a day of severe hunger﴾: "a day on which food is desired."

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from 'Uthman al-Thaqafi, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿on a day of severe hunger﴾, he said: "famine."

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from 'Uthman ibn al-Mughirah, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, the like of it.

I was told from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: ﴿on a day of severe hunger﴾, he said: "famine."

* *

His saying: ﴿an orphan of near relationship﴾

He says: or feeding on a day of famine a child who has no father from among his relatives, and he is the orphan of near relationship; by "one of near relationship" is meant one of kinship.

As it was narrated:

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: ﴿an orphan of near relationship﴾, he said: "one of kinship."

* *

His saying: ﴿or a needy person in misery﴾

The people of interpretation differed regarding the interpretation of His saying: ﴿one in misery﴾. Some of them said: By it is meant one clinging to the dust.

Mention of those who said that:

Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi 'Adiy narrated to us, from Shu'bah, who said: al-Mughirah informed me, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿or a needy person in misery﴾, he said: "The one who has no shelter except the dust."

Mutarrif ibn Muhammad al-Dabbi narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from al-Mughirah, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, the like of it.

Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi 'Adiy narrated to us, from Shu'bah, from Husayn, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding God's saying: ﴿or a needy person in misery﴾, he said: "The one whom none but the dust covers."

Zakariyya ibn Yahya ibn Abi Za'idah narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, from Shu'bah, from al-Mughirah, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿one in misery﴾, he said: "The one who has no shelter except the dust."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 90, verse 8–16 (part 2 of 2):

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Jarir related to me, from Mughira, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿a needy person in misery﴾: he said: "the one who has no shelter except the dust."

⁕ He said: Jarir related to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words: ﴿or a needy person in misery﴾: he said: "The needy one; the one cast down in the dust."

⁕ Abu Husayn related to me, saying: Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Yunus related to us, saying: Abthar related to us, from Husayn, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, his words: ﴿or a needy person in misery﴾: he said: "The one whom nothing protects from the dust."

⁕ Ya'qub related to me, saying: Hushaym related to us, saying: Husayn and Mughira both related to us, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, that he said concerning His words: ﴿or a needy person in misery﴾: he said: "He is the one clinging to the dust because of extreme poverty."

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Hakkam related to us, from Amr ibn Abi Qays, from Mansur, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿or a needy person in misery﴾: he said: "The dust thrown on the road, on the refuse heap."

⁕ Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Talq ibn Ghanam related to us, from Za'ida, from Mansur, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿or a needy person in misery﴾: he said: "He is the needy one cast onto the road in the dust."

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Husayn, from Mujahid: ﴿or a needy person in misery﴾: he said: "The one cast down on the earth, whom nothing protects from the dust."

⁕ Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, from Sufyan, from Husayn, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿or a needy person in misery﴾: he said: "He is the one pressed to the earth, whom nothing protects from the dust."

⁕ Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Husayn and Uthman ibn al-Mughira, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿or a needy person in misery﴾: he said: "The one who has nothing to protect him from the dust."

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, his words: ﴿in misery﴾: he said: "Fallen in the dust."

⁕ Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, from Ja'far ibn Burqan, who said: Ikrima heard ﴿or a needy person in misery﴾, and said: "The one clinging to the earth from need."
